subtitle: A corporate-feudal galaxy where information is the scarcest commodity.

milestones.title: Foundations
milestones.goal: A deterministic headless sim and a real-scale planet you can fly to and from.
milestones.gate: Read out/world-dump.txt: can you trace a corporate collapse back four causes, and do two NPCs disagree about the same fact for legible reasons? Separately: does the client fly orbit to ground to orbit with no loading screen?

evidence.caption: 6,371 km planet from 2 radii: oceans, coastlines, atmospheric limb
Eroded terrain from 1.2 km: triplanar detail, volumetric cloud deck
The town: 32 buildings, 342 trees, ship on the pad
Back in orbit after climbing through the ship's own flight model
Phase 0 gate artifact: 50,000 ticks, causal chains, metrics

milestones.title: Terrain to production standard
milestones.goal: The terrain stops being a spike: water, stable LOD, collision everywhere it is needed, and assets that survive a cook.
milestones.gate: Fly a 200 km transect at 300 m altitude at 60 fps with no holes, no popping that reads as a seam, and no frame over 20 ms.

milestones.title: Surface fidelity
milestones.goal: Ground that holds up at walking distance: biome-blended materials, real texture sets, and detail that survives every LOD transition.
milestones.gate: Stand on the surface at three biomes and at three altitudes. No tiling is visible, no shimmer, and the material does not change identity when a patch splits.

milestones.title: Ship systems and flight
milestones.goal: A ship you can actually fly: cockpit, HUD, landing gear, fuel, damage, and a flight model that behaves in vacuum and in air.
milestones.gate: Take off from the pad, reach orbit, re-enter, and land on the same pad using only the cockpit view and the HUD.

milestones.title: Sim to client bridge
milestones.goal: The client stops reading a file. protobuf over TCP, live world state, and a contract board that reflects the running simulation.
milestones.gate: Kill the sim mid-flight: the client degrades visibly and recovers when it restarts, without a crash and without inventing state.

milestones.title: The bounty loop, end to end
milestones.goal: Design SS4.2's canonical mission, built properly: accept, investigate by disclosure, narrow a search volume, locate physically, resolve, choose delivery.
milestones.gate: Phase 1 gate (SS13.2): does the bounty feel like investigation rather than a quest marker? Can a player describe how they found the target?

milestones.title: Narration
milestones.goal: A local model that renders state into prose and selects from a closed action space. It never decides anything that matters.
milestones.gate: Tier 5: a full sim run with narration stubbed produces byte-identical world state to one with narration live.

milestones.title: Economy and the news feed
milestones.goal: Markets that move because something happened, and a news feed that is a lossy, biased rendering of true underlying state.
milestones.gate: Watch a convoy die, then trade on it before the article appears. The article, when it appears, is late and slightly wrong.

milestones.title: Crew
milestones.goal: Named, simulated people you hire, rely on, and can lose. The losable thing (SS2.1).
milestones.gate: Lose a crew member to a chain of events that was your fault and was foreseeable, and be able to reconstruct the chain afterwards.

milestones.title: All six mission archetypes
milestones.goal: Audit, Interception, Extraction, Fabrication and Collection, all on the one hidden-variable algorithm. No second implementation.
milestones.gate: SS12 oatmeal detector: no archetype exceeds 35% of generated contracts over a 10,000 tick run, and every one uses the same investigation code path.

milestones.title: Simulation LOD and reification
milestones.goal: A world that ticks statistically where nobody is watching and instantiates consistently when somebody arrives.
milestones.gate: Property test: aggregate(reify(A)) == A for arbitrary aggregate state. And a player cannot find the seam by flying between regions.

milestones.title: Multiplayer foundation
milestones.goal: A 16 to 32 player shard, sim-authoritative, with the PvPvE persistence classes resolved and IP counsel's review complete.
milestones.gate: Sixteen players on one shard for an hour. No desync, no duplicated bounty target, and the belief graph survives a coordinated rumour-injection attempt.

milestones.title: MVP gate
milestones.goal: The four pillar tests, on a live build, with real players.
milestones.gate: P1: log out for a week, find three causally-explicable changes. P2: reconstruct four causes of any world change. P3: two players hold contradictory sincere beliefs. P4: lose something you spent twenty hours building, foreseeably.

tasks.title: Rust workspace and CI-ready sim crate
tasks.detail: Scaffold sim/ as a zero-dependency Rust crate. Event log, deterministic fold, seeded PRNG, fixed-point arithmetic.
tasks.acceptance: cargo test green on an empty suite; replay determinism test exists before any domain logic.

tasks.title: Fixed-point arithmetic with no floats in authoritative state
tasks.detail: Fx as scaled i64 with i128 intermediates. Display, clamp, exact rational scaling.
tasks.acceptance: Multiplication at 1e12 does not overflow; display is stable and signed.

tasks.title: Deterministic PRNG seeded per region per tick
tasks.detail: SplitMix64 derived from (world_seed, region_id, tick). Never thread_rng.
tasks.acceptance: Same seed gives the same sequence; adjacent ticks and regions do not correlate.

tasks.title: Event log and the fold
tasks.detail: Append-only log; World::apply is the only write path; every event carries its cause.
tasks.acceptance: Causal chain walks back and terminates; every cause points at an earlier event.

tasks.title: Belief graph with propagation, decay and distortion
tasks.detail: Typed Proposition enum, Belief with confidence and provenance, single-hop propagation.
tasks.acceptance: Confidence never rises without independent corroboration; propagation terminates on a cyclic social graph.

tasks.title: Disposition computed, never stored
tasks.detail: Disposition is a pure function of an entity's belief set. No reputation field anywhere.
tasks.acceptance: grep the codebase for a stored reputation or relationship scalar: zero hits.

tasks.title: Obligation ledger as a consumed-on-redemption multigraph
tasks.detail: Typed ObligationClass; favours are spent, not renewable.
tasks.acceptance: A redeemed favour cannot be redeemed twice; ordering is deterministic.

tasks.title: Investigation algorithm with search volumes
tasks.detail: Search volume over a hidden variable; disclosures constrain it; contradictions widen it.
tasks.acceptance: A contradictory claim widens the volume rather than silently picking a winner.

tasks.title: Economy with conservation laws
tasks.detail: Cash and territory move between corps, never evaporate. Mean-reversion via overhead.
tasks.acceptance: Money supply and lane count constant over 20,000 ticks; no faction ossifies.

tasks.title: Mission generation as a query over existing tension
tasks.detail: find (A,B) where A holds unresolved obligation against B and the tension predates the query.
tasks.acceptance: Over 90% of contracts reference tension incurred before they were posted.

tasks.title: Text world-dump and the SS12 metrics
tasks.detail: A readable log of what happened and why, with the metrics printed into it.
tasks.acceptance: A corporate collapse can be traced back four causes from the dump alone.

tasks.title: Tier 2 and Tier 4 test suites
tasks.detail: Invariant property tests and bit-identical replay determinism.
tasks.acceptance: 69 tests green; replay from the same seed is identical, from a different seed is not.

tasks.title: UE5 C++ client with a typed snapshot boundary
tasks.detail: No Blueprint logic. Archetypes parse into a UENUM; unknown variants are a parse failure.
tasks.acceptance: Six automation tests pass headless via UnrealEditor-Cmd.

tasks.title: Cube-sphere quadtree terrain with screen-space error LOD
tasks.detail: Six roots, horizon culling, edge-index stitching, vertices relative to node centres.
tasks.acceptance: A planet renders from orbit with no cracks at face seams.

tasks.title: Move patch generation to worker threads
tasks.detail: Free functions over copied inputs; the game thread only uploads.
tasks.acceptance: Worst game-thread cost falls from 53 ms to under 8 ms; zero starved patches at altitude.

tasks.title: Scale the planet to 6,371 km
tasks.detail: Real radius, MaxDepth 15, noise frequency bands rescaled to the circumference.
tasks.acceptance: 4.8 m quads at the finest LOD; LWC carries the coordinates without precision loss.

tasks.title: Sky Atmosphere, volumetric clouds, ozone
tasks.detail: Earth's own scattering values at Earth's radius. Height fog removed as flat-world.
tasks.acceptance: Sky is black outside the atmosphere and blue from the ground, with no parameter fighting.

tasks.title: Analytic erosion via slope-damped octaves
tasks.detail: Exact noise derivatives; each octave damped by the accumulated slope above it.
tasks.acceptance: Terrain shows drainage. No seams at LOD boundaries, because it is a pure function.

tasks.title: Triplanar surface material from generated mipped textures
tasks.detail: 256px detail textures with a full mip chain; world-aligned projection; depth fade.
tasks.acceptance: No aliasing at any distance; no UV seam anywhere on the sphere.

tasks.title: Ship, gravity, and a town
tasks.detail: 6-DOF flight, inverse-square gravity, atmospheric drag; 32 buildings and 342 trees.
tasks.acceptance: The ship lands under gravity and climbs back to orbit through its own flight model.

tasks.title: ADR-0001 and ADR-0002
tasks.detail: Stack decision and the terrain build-vs-buy decision, with measurements attached.
tasks.acceptance: Both ADRs are in docs/adr with Context, Decision, Consequences and rejected alternatives.

tasks.title: Water surface as a separate render pass
tasks.detail: Oceans are currently coloured terrain. Build a sea-level shell mesh with its own material: depth-based colour, Fresnel, and a screen-space reflection fallback.
tasks.acceptance: Standing on a beach, the waterline is a surface with a horizon, not a colour change.

notes.text: Water rides the terrain quadtree as mesh section 1, inheriting its LOD; quads emitted only where a corner is below sea level
Bug: VertexColor pin 0 is float3 RGB, so masking it for alpha failed to compile. UE logs one line and silently swaps the default material, so every edit to the water shader appeared to do nothing
opaque water, depth-tinted from vertex alpha, Fresnel, SSR-compatible roughness

evidence.caption: Waterline at a shoreline: turquoise shallows, deeper channel, sand — a surface with a horizon
Ocean from orbit with specular sun glint and depth gradient

tasks.title: Wave displacement and shoreline foam
tasks.detail: Gerstner waves in the water material, amplitude falling off in shallow water. Foam where the terrain approaches sea level.
tasks.acceptance: Waves are visible from 200 m and flatten correctly against the shore.

tasks.title: Underwater fog and camera transition
tasks.detail: A post-process volume that engages when the camera crosses the waterline.
tasks.acceptance: Flying into the sea transitions without a pop and back out without a flash.

tasks.title: Ocean-floor terrain profile
tasks.detail: Seabeds currently use one smoothing rule. Add continental shelf, slope and abyssal plain so the depth profile reads as bathymetry.
tasks.acceptance: A cross-section from coast to deep ocean shows a shelf break.

tasks.title: Patch cache keyed by node id
tasks.detail: Regenerating a patch the camera just left is pure waste. LRU cache of recent vertex buffers, bounded by memory not count.
tasks.acceptance: Flying back and forth across a ridge regenerates nothing after the first pass.

tasks.title: Predictive patch prefetch along the velocity vector
tasks.detail: The collision cook already leads the camera. Do the same for geometry so a fast approach arrives at ground that already exists.
tasks.acceptance: A 300 m/s descent shows no unfilled patches at any point.

tasks.title: LOD transition blending
tasks.detail: Patches currently swap. Blend between levels over a short distance band using vertex morphing toward the parent's surface.
tasks.acceptance: No visible pop at any LOD boundary during a continuous descent.

tasks.title: Fix stitching for the finer-neighbour case
tasks.detail: Stitching only collapses vertices on the fine side. Verify the coarse side never needs it, and add a test that walks every visible edge pair.
tasks.acceptance: An automated test finds zero cracks over 500 randomised camera positions.

tasks.title: Collision for the town footprint and landing pads
tasks.detail: Terrain collision is camera-radius only. Pin collision permanently around persistent structures so a ship cannot fall through an unloaded patch.
tasks.acceptance: Teleport to the pad from orbit: the ship rests on it immediately.

tasks.title: Collision cook budget and instrumentation
tasks.detail: Track cook time per frame and per patch; alert in the stats when the budget is exceeded.
tasks.acceptance: Ledger.Terrain.Stats reports cook time distribution, not just the worst case.

tasks.title: Save generated terrain material as a real asset
tasks.detail: The material is built at runtime and therefore editor-only. Write an editor commandlet that builds it once and saves it to /Game/Materials.
tasks.acceptance: A packaged build renders the terrain correctly with no runtime shader compilation.

tasks.title: Save generated detail textures as assets
tasks.detail: Same problem, same fix: generate the mipped textures at cook time.
tasks.acceptance: The packaged build ships the textures; no UTexture2D is created at runtime.

tasks.title: Package a standalone game build
tasks.detail: The game target links but has never been cooked. Get a packaged build running.
tasks.acceptance: Ledger.exe runs the reentry sequence with no editor present.

tasks.title: Gauntlet performance test for the descent
tasks.detail: Automate the orbit-to-ground descent as a Gauntlet test that records frame times.
tasks.acceptance: The test fails if any frame exceeds 20 ms or the 99th percentile exceeds 16.6 ms.

tasks.title: Terrain unit tests for the maths layer
tasks.detail: LedgerTerrainMath has no tests. Cover cube-sphere round-tripping, noise determinism, derivative correctness against finite differences, and screen-space error.
tasks.acceptance: Analytic derivatives agree with central differences to 1e-6 over 10,000 samples.

tasks.title: Deterministic terrain across machines
tasks.detail: The terrain is a pure function of a seed, so two machines must agree. Hash a grid of elevation samples and compare in CI.
tasks.acceptance: The elevation hash is identical on two machines and across two builds.

tasks.title: Profile and reduce per-patch generation cost
tasks.detail: Erosion doubled the sample cost. Profile the noise inner loop and cut it: cache gradients, hoist the hash, consider SIMD.
tasks.acceptance: Patch generation falls below 4 ms for a 65x65 patch with erosion on.

tasks.title: Bound the mesh component pool by memory
tasks.detail: The pool is a fixed 2,560 components. Size it against a memory budget and report when it is the limiting factor.
tasks.acceptance: Stats show whether the pool or the job queue is the binding constraint.

tasks.title: Horizon culling correctness test
tasks.detail: Culling silently disabled itself once already. Add a test that asserts the visible set matches a brute-force horizon check at many altitudes.
tasks.acceptance: Culled set matches brute force at 12 altitudes from surface to 3 radii.

tasks.title: Terrain streaming under a moving observer, soak test
tasks.detail: Fly a great-circle route for 30 minutes and assert no leak, no starvation, no crack.
tasks.acceptance: Memory is flat after the first orbit; zero starved patches; zero cracks.

tasks.title: M1 evidence: transect flight recording
tasks.detail: Capture the 200 km transect with frame times overlaid.
tasks.acceptance: Video and frame-time trace uploaded as milestone evidence.

tasks.title: GitHub Actions: sim suite on every commit
tasks.detail: Design SS9 says the sim suite runs on every commit and UE builds nightly. Wire it.
tasks.acceptance: A push runs cargo test and fails the check on a red test.

tasks.title: GitHub Actions: nightly UE build and automation tests
tasks.detail: Build the editor target and run the Tier 6 suite headless on a schedule.
tasks.acceptance: A nightly run produces a build artifact and a test report.

tasks.title: Nightly Tier 3 fuzz job
tasks.detail: The 1,000,000 tick invariant run, nightly, with failure notification.
tasks.acceptance: A deliberately broken invariant is caught by the next nightly run.

tasks.title: Terrain debug visualisation modes
tasks.detail: Wireframe, LOD level as colour, patch age, collision coverage.
tasks.acceptance: Ledger.Terrain.Debug cycles the modes and each is legible.

tasks.title: Frame-time HUD and stat capture
tasks.detail: A permanent overlay recording frame time, patch queue and memory.
tasks.acceptance: Any capture can be correlated with the frame cost at that moment.

tasks.title: Crash reporting and symbol retention
tasks.detail: Keep PDBs per build so a crash from a week-old build is still readable.
tasks.acceptance: A stack from an archived build resolves to source lines.

tasks.title: Biome classification from climate rather than altitude
tasks.detail: Colour is keyed to height and slope. Derive latitude, temperature and moisture from position and circulation, then classify biome from those.
tasks.acceptance: A desert appears in a rain shadow, not at a fixed altitude band.

tasks.title: Author a texture set per biome
tasks.detail: Albedo, normal, roughness and height for rock, sand, grass, forest floor, snow.
tasks.acceptance: Five biomes, each with four maps, all generated procedurally and cooked as assets.

tasks.title: Height-blended material layering
tasks.detail: Blend biomes by their height maps rather than by linear interpolation, so transitions interlock instead of dissolving.
tasks.acceptance: A grass-to-rock transition shows grass in the crevices and rock on the high points.

tasks.title: Parallax occlusion on the near LOD
tasks.detail: Give close ground depth without geometry, faded out past 30 m.
tasks.acceptance: Standing still, the ground has relief below the vertex scale; no cost past 30 m.

tasks.title: Distance-based macro variation
tasks.detail: Break the tiling that shows up from the air with a low-frequency colour and roughness modulation driven by the same noise the terrain uses.
tasks.acceptance: From 2 km, no repeating pattern is visible anywhere in frame.

tasks.title: Triplanar seam reduction on steep slopes
tasks.detail: The three projections blend by normal; sharpen the blend so cliffs do not smear.
tasks.acceptance: A vertical cliff face shows one dominant projection, not three overlapping.

tasks.title: Material LOD continuity across patch splits
tasks.detail: A patch split must not change material identity. Drive everything from world position, never from patch UVs.
tasks.acceptance: Recording a split at 60 fps shows no material change on the frame the split happens.

tasks.title: Runtime Virtual Texture evaluation for the surface
tasks.detail: Design SS6.8 proposes RVT. Prototype six RVT volumes on the cube faces and measure against the current triplanar path.
tasks.acceptance: An ADR recording whether RVT beats triplanar here, with measurements.

tasks.title: Snow and sand accumulation by slope and exposure
tasks.detail: Deposit on shallow slopes and lee faces, expose rock on steep and windward.
tasks.acceptance: Snow lies in gullies and off cliff faces without being authored.

tasks.title: Wetness near the waterline and in valley floors
tasks.detail: Darken albedo and drop roughness where drainage accumulates.
tasks.acceptance: River valleys read as wet without a water mesh in them.

tasks.title: Ambient occlusion baked into vertex colour
tasks.detail: Approximate AO from the local heightfield curvature at generation time.
tasks.acceptance: Valleys and crevices darken correctly with no screen-space cost.

tasks.title: Scatter rocks and vegetation by biome
tasks.detail: Instanced meshes placed from the same deterministic rules the biome uses.
tasks.acceptance: Ten thousand instances within 500 m at no measurable frame cost.

tasks.title: Procedural rock and plant meshes
tasks.detail: Extend the mesh builder: rocks by displaced icosphere, shrubs and grass by billboard clusters.
tasks.acceptance: Six rock variants and four plant variants, all generated from a seed.

tasks.title: Vegetation wind animation
tasks.detail: World-position-offset in the material, driven by a global wind vector.
tasks.acceptance: Grass and canopies move coherently; nothing is animated per-instance on the CPU.

tasks.title: Material parameter collection for global look
tasks.detail: One collection holding wind, wetness, season and time of day, so the whole surface can be retuned without touching every material.
tasks.acceptance: Changing one parameter changes the whole planet's look consistently.

tasks.title: Surface fidelity soak test
tasks.detail: Fly a route through every biome at three altitudes and capture stills.
tasks.acceptance: Fifteen stills, no tiling, no shimmer, no material identity change.

tasks.title: M2 evidence: biome gallery
tasks.detail: Capture each biome at walking distance, at 200 m and from orbit.
tasks.acceptance: Gallery uploaded as milestone evidence.

tasks.title: Screenshot regression harness
tasks.detail: Capture fixed viewpoints each nightly build and diff against a baseline.
tasks.acceptance: A material change that alters the look is flagged automatically.

tasks.title: Material complexity budget
tasks.detail: Shader instruction counts tracked per material, with a ceiling.
tasks.acceptance: Exceeding the ceiling fails the nightly build.

tasks.title: Texture memory budget and streaming
tasks.detail: Know what the surface costs in VRAM, and leave room for the narration model.
tasks.acceptance: Surface textures stay under budget with 4 GB reserved for inference.

tasks.title: Colour grading and tone mapping pass
tasks.detail: One look, applied consistently, rather than per-scene exposure fiddling.
tasks.acceptance: The same grade reads correctly in orbit, at altitude and on the ground.

tasks.title: Time of day and a moving sun
tasks.detail: The sun currently never moves. Drive it from sim time.
tasks.acceptance: A full day-night cycle runs and the atmosphere responds correctly at dawn.

tasks.title: Night side: stars, moonlight, and town lights
tasks.detail: The dark half of the planet has to be worth flying over.
tasks.acceptance: Town lights are visible from orbit on the night side.

tasks.title: Parametric ship kit with typed socket interfaces
tasks.detail: Design SS6.9's ~40 components. Hull sections, wings, nacelles, gear, sensors, each with a typed socket, assembled at editor time and baked to StaticMesh.
tasks.acceptance: Three hulls generated from the same kit by changing parameters only.

tasks.title: Editor tooling for ship assembly
tasks.detail: A commandlet that builds a hull from a parameter set and saves the asset.
tasks.acceptance: Changing hull_length from 24 m to 18 m regenerates in seconds.

tasks.title: Cockpit interior and first-person view
tasks.detail: Cockpit-only interiors per SS6.9. Seat, canopy frame, instrument panel geometry.
tasks.acceptance: The cockpit view shows a frame and panel that occlude correctly against the world.

tasks.title: Flight HUD: attitude, velocity, altitude, throttle
tasks.detail: Drawn in C++ via Slate or a HUD class, no UMG assets.
tasks.acceptance: Altitude reads correctly from orbit to ground; the horizon indicator is right at every point on the sphere.

tasks.title: Navigation and target reticle
tasks.detail: A marker for the selected destination that works in a spherical frame.
tasks.acceptance: The town marker stays correct while flying around the planet.

tasks.title: Landing gear with deployment and ground contact
tasks.detail: Gear geometry, animation, and per-leg ground contact rather than a single point.
tasks.acceptance: The ship rests level on a slope, on three legs, without sinking.

tasks.title: Fuel and thrust budget
tasks.detail: Delta-v as a resource. Burn on main thrust, drain faster in atmosphere.
tasks.acceptance: Reaching orbit from sea level consumes a legible fraction of a full tank.

tasks.title: Atmospheric heating on re-entry
tasks.detail: Heat accumulation from velocity and density, with a visual effect and a damage threshold.
tasks.acceptance: A steep fast re-entry damages the hull; a shallow one does not.

tasks.title: Hull damage model
tasks.detail: Component-level damage: engines, control surfaces, hull integrity.
tasks.acceptance: Losing an engine changes the flight model asymmetrically.

tasks.title: Flight assist modes
tasks.detail: Full 6-DOF for vacuum, an atmospheric assist that holds attitude against gravity.
tasks.acceptance: Assist on, the ship holds a hover; assist off, it does not.

tasks.title: Ship-relative camera modes
tasks.detail: Chase, cockpit, and an external orbit camera, all correct in a spherical frame.
tasks.acceptance: No camera mode gimbal-locks at any point on the planet.

tasks.title: Engine and thruster visual effects
tasks.detail: Niagara plumes scaled by throttle, with atmospheric versus vacuum behaviour.
tasks.acceptance: Plumes shorten and widen in atmosphere and go pencil-thin in vacuum.

tasks.title: Sound: engines, atmosphere, and its absence
tasks.detail: Procedural engine tone by throttle, wind noise by dynamic pressure, silence in vacuum.
tasks.acceptance: Crossing the Karman line, wind noise fades to nothing while the engine stays.

tasks.title: Docking and landing pad interaction
tasks.detail: Detect a valid landing, lock the ship, and expose an interaction prompt.
tasks.acceptance: Landing on the pad within tolerance registers; landing beside it does not.

tasks.title: Ship save and restore state
tasks.detail: Position, orientation, velocity, fuel and damage persist across a session boundary.
tasks.acceptance: Quit in orbit, restart, and the ship is where it was, in the state it was.

tasks.title: Flight model unit tests
tasks.detail: Gravity, drag and thrust as pure functions, tested without a world.
tasks.acceptance: Orbital velocity at 200 km matches the analytic value to within 1%.

tasks.title: M3 evidence: cockpit round trip
tasks.detail: Record a full pad-to-orbit-to-pad flight from the cockpit view.
tasks.acceptance: Recording uploaded as milestone evidence.

tasks.title: Input remapping and gamepad support
tasks.detail: Axis mappings are hard-coded in config. Support rebinding and a controller.
tasks.acceptance: A gamepad flies the ship with no keyboard input.

tasks.title: Settings menu in C++
tasks.detail: Resolution, quality, input, audio. No UMG assets.
tasks.acceptance: Settings persist across a restart.

tasks.title: Pause, save and quit flow
tasks.detail: A session boundary that does not lose state.
tasks.acceptance: Quitting and resuming restores the ship and the world clock.

tasks.title: Ship interior ambient audio
tasks.detail: Hull creak under load, air handling, alarm tones on damage.
tasks.acceptance: Damage produces an audible cue before the HUD shows it.

tasks.title: Accessibility: subtitles, colourblind-safe HUD, motion options
tasks.detail: The HUD encodes state in colour alone in places. Fix that.
tasks.acceptance: Every HUD state is distinguishable without colour.

tasks.title: proto/ schema for the wire contract
tasks.detail: Design SS10: proto/ is the only place the sim-client contract is defined, and both sides generate from it. Entities, factions, contracts, beliefs, market state.
tasks.acceptance: Both the Rust sim and the UE client build from the same .proto with no hand-written duplicate of any message.

tasks.title: Rust protobuf codegen in the sim build
tasks.detail: prost or equivalent, wired into build.rs so the generated types are never committed.
tasks.acceptance: Deleting the generated directory and rebuilding produces identical types.

tasks.title: UE protobuf integration as a third-party module
tasks.detail: The known slog: UE disables exceptions and RTTI, and its check macro collides with protobuf headers. Budget it explicitly.
tasks.acceptance: The client links protobuf and round-trips a message in an automation test.

tasks.title: Length-prefixed TCP transport
tasks.detail: Phase 1 transport per ADR-0001. Framing, reconnect with backoff, and a heartbeat.
tasks.acceptance: Killing the sim and restarting it reconnects within two seconds with no client restart.

tasks.title: Sim-side gRPC-free server loop
tasks.detail: A tick loop that accepts connections, streams state deltas, and applies client intents.
tasks.acceptance: One client connected costs under 0.5 ms per tick of server time.

tasks.title: World state delta encoding
tasks.detail: Send what changed, not the world. Per-entity dirty flags folded from the event log.
tasks.acceptance: Steady-state bandwidth under 32 KB/s per client with 2,000 entities simulated.

tasks.title: Client-side world state cache and interpolation
tasks.detail: The client holds a view of sim state and interpolates between ticks for presentation.
tasks.acceptance: Entity positions do not jitter at a 10 Hz sim tick and a 60 Hz render.

tasks.title: Contract board reading live sim state
tasks.detail: Replace the snapshot file. The board reflects contracts as they are posted.
tasks.acceptance: A contract posted in the sim appears on the board within one tick round trip.

tasks.title: Player intent messages
tasks.detail: Accept a contract, make an inquiry, offer an incentive, redeem a favour. Typed, validated server-side.
tasks.acceptance: A malformed or impossible intent is rejected with a typed error, never applied.

tasks.title: Schema versioning and refusal
tasks.detail: The client already refuses a future snapshot schema. Extend that to the wire protocol.
tasks.acceptance: A client one version behind refuses to connect and says why.

tasks.title: Connection state in the UI
tasks.detail: Show connected, reconnecting, and stale-state clearly rather than silently lying.
tasks.acceptance: Killing the sim shows a visible degraded state within two seconds.

tasks.title: Sim as a service: run headless, log, restart
tasks.detail: Process supervision, structured logging, and a clean shutdown that flushes the log.
tasks.acceptance: SIGTERM produces a replayable log with no truncated event.

tasks.title: Event log persistence to disk
tasks.detail: ADR-0001 defers Postgres; this is the file-backed step before it. Append-only, chunked, with a manifest.
tasks.acceptance: A 1,000,000 tick run writes a log that replays to a bit-identical state.

tasks.title: Replay bisector tool
tasks.detail: Design SS11 wants this early. Replay to tick N, bisect for the first divergence.
tasks.acceptance: Given a seeded divergence, the bisector finds the exact event in under a minute.

tasks.title: World inspector tool
tasks.detail: A text or web view of live sim state: entities, beliefs, obligations, market.
tasks.acceptance: Any entity's full belief set is inspectable while the sim runs.

tasks.title: Bridge integration tests
tasks.detail: Sim and client in one test harness, asserting state agreement after N ticks.
tasks.acceptance: Client and sim agree on every contract and corp balance after 1,000 ticks.

tasks.title: M4 evidence: kill-the-sim recording
tasks.detail: Record the client degrading and recovering.
tasks.acceptance: Recording uploaded as milestone evidence.

tasks.title: OpenTelemetry instrumentation in the sim
tasks.detail: SS9's observability stack, now that there is a service to observe.
tasks.acceptance: Per-region tick cost and propagation depth export as metrics.

tasks.title: Grafana dashboards for the SS12 metrics
tasks.detail: Every metric in SS12 on one board, with its target band drawn on.
tasks.acceptance: A metric outside its band is visually obvious without reading numbers.

tasks.title: Structured logging with correlation ids
tasks.detail: Trace an intent from client to sim to event to consequence.
tasks.acceptance: One id follows a contract acceptance through every log line it causes.

tasks.title: Deployment scripts for the sim service
tasks.detail: SS10's ops/ tree. Run it somewhere that is not a developer laptop.
tasks.acceptance: The sim runs on a remote host and a local client connects to it.

tasks.title: Database migration path from file log to Postgres
tasks.detail: ADR-0001 defers this to Phase 1. This is Phase 1.
tasks.acceptance: The same event log replays identically from a file and from Postgres.

tasks.title: Contract board UI with archetype and tension age
tasks.detail: Show who wants what, and how old the grudge is. The age is what makes it read as authored rather than generated.
tasks.acceptance: Every listed contract shows the tick its tension was incurred.

tasks.title: Accept and abandon a contract
tasks.detail: Acceptance is an event that propagates. Abandoning has a cost.
tasks.acceptance: Accepting a contract is visible to other entities through the belief graph.

tasks.title: NPC entities rendered in the world
tasks.detail: Simulated people need bodies where the player is. Instanced characters placed from sim state, at the region the sim says they are in.
tasks.acceptance: An NPC the sim moves is seen to move, without a teleport.

tasks.title: Approach and conversation entry
tasks.detail: Walk or fly to an NPC and open a conversation. No dialogue content yet.
tasks.acceptance: Conversation opens against the correct simulated entity, identified by id.

tasks.title: Disclosure interaction: the four incentives
tasks.detail: Money, favour redemption, threat, and traded information, per SS6.3.
tasks.acceptance: Each incentive produces a different disclosure probability, visibly.

tasks.title: Search volume rendered as a region, not a pin
tasks.detail: SS6.3 is explicit: no quest markers. Draw the volume as a shaded region on the map and in the world.
tasks.acceptance: The volume visibly widens when a source contradicts an earlier one.

tasks.title: Inquiry events propagate and the target reacts
tasks.detail: The closing edge of the core loop. Asking is itself an event.
tasks.acceptance: Asking enough people causes the target to relocate, traceably.

tasks.title: Stale intelligence and the cost of delay
tasks.detail: A disclosure ages. Its confidence decays, and acting on old information fails.
tasks.acceptance: Waiting ten in-game days after a disclosure makes the location wrong.

tasks.title: Physical resolution: locating the target on the surface
tasks.detail: Fly to the region, find the target's actual position, and approach.
tasks.acceptance: The target is physically present at the location the sim holds, not spawned on arrival.

tasks.title: Capture alive versus kill
tasks.detail: Alive is worth more and requires approach and preparation. Dead is fast and loud.
tasks.acceptance: Killing generates worse events than capturing, measurably, in the belief graph.

tasks.title: Delivery choice and betrayal
tasks.detail: The posting corp is not the only buyer. A rival may pay more.
tasks.acceptance: Delivering to the rival is a betrayal event that propagates and changes disposition.

tasks.title: Consequence surfacing after the fact
tasks.detail: Show the player what their choice caused, days later, without telling them at the time.
tasks.acceptance: A betrayal produces a visible consequence at least one session later.

tasks.title: Witness system and elimination
tasks.detail: Who saw what, and what happens if they do not survive to tell it.
tasks.acceptance: Removing the only witness measurably slows propagation of the act.

tasks.title: Map view with belief overlay
tasks.detail: Show what the player knows, not what is true. Confidence and provenance visible.
tasks.acceptance: The map shows a contradicted location as two claims, not an average.

tasks.title: Journal of leads and sources
tasks.detail: A record of who said what, when, and how sure they were.
tasks.acceptance: A player can reconstruct how they found a target from the journal alone.

tasks.title: Scripted agent parity test
tasks.detail: The headless scripted agent and the player-facing loop must exercise the same code.
tasks.acceptance: A test drives the full loop headlessly and asserts the same events as a play session.

tasks.title: Bounty loop balance pass
tasks.detail: Tune disclosure costs, decay rates and flight thresholds against the SS12 bands.
tasks.acceptance: Favour redemption 40-70%, false beliefs 10-25%, propagation depth 3-6 hops.

tasks.title: M5 evidence: a bounty, start to finish
tasks.detail: Record a full contract from board to delivery, with the journal visible.
tasks.acceptance: Recording plus journal export uploaded as milestone evidence.

tasks.title: Tutorial-free onboarding
tasks.detail: The first contract has to teach the loop without a tutorial, because the loop is the game and a tutorial would tell you the answer.
tasks.acceptance: A new player completes a first contract without instructions, in a playtest.

tasks.title: Playtest harness and session recording
tasks.detail: Record inputs and sim state so a playtest can be replayed and analysed.
tasks.acceptance: A recorded session replays deterministically.

tasks.title: First external playtest
tasks.detail: Five people who have not seen it. Watch, do not explain.
tasks.acceptance: Written notes from five sessions, with the points where players stalled.

tasks.title: Investigation UI iteration from playtest findings
tasks.detail: Fix whatever the playtest showed, not whatever seemed likely beforehand.
tasks.acceptance: The top three stall points from the playtest are addressed and retested.

tasks.title: Narration service skeleton in Python
tasks.detail: Design SS10's narration/ tree. A process that accepts structured state and returns text or an enum, batched and off the critical path.
tasks.acceptance: The sim runs identically with the service absent.

tasks.title: llama.cpp integration with a quantised local model
tasks.detail: 3-8B at Q4 per SS6.4, with an explicit VRAM budget measured against the renderer.
tasks.acceptance: Inference runs alongside a 60 fps render without dropping frames.

tasks.title: GBNF grammars for constrained action selection
tasks.detail: The model selects an enum variant, never free text that touches state.
tasks.acceptance: Every model output parses into a typed variant or is rejected; zero string parsing.

tasks.title: Renderers: news article from market state
tasks.detail: State to prose. The article is a lossy, biased rendering of true state.
tasks.acceptance: Articles lag the price move that caused them.

tasks.title: Renderers: dialogue line from disposition and belief
tasks.detail: What an NPC says derives from what it believes and how it feels, both computed.
tasks.acceptance: Two NPCs with contradictory beliefs say contradictory things.

tasks.title: Renderers: corporate filings and obligation notices
tasks.detail: Bureaucratic menace as text. The scariest thing in the setting is a compliance division.
tasks.acceptance: A filing references a real obligation with real numbers from the ledger.

tasks.title: Authored fallback lines on timeout
tasks.detail: 300 ms budget per SS6.4, with a fallback that is never obviously a fallback.
tasks.acceptance: Forcing every request to time out still produces a playable conversation.

tasks.title: Batching and scheduling off the render thread
tasks.detail: Slow decisions only: faction moves on minutes, board text at refresh, dialogue at open.
tasks.acceptance: No inference call is made from the render thread, ever, asserted in code.

tasks.title: Tier 5 stub-equivalence test
tasks.detail: A full sim run with narration stubbed must produce byte-identical world state.
tasks.acceptance: The test is in CI and fails if any narration path writes to authoritative state.

tasks.title: Prompt and grammar versioning
tasks.detail: Prompts are code. Version them, and record which version produced which text.
tasks.acceptance: Any generated article can be traced to the prompt and model version that made it.

tasks.title: Narration cost and latency dashboard
tasks.detail: Measure tokens, latency and fallback rate per surface.
tasks.acceptance: Fallback rate is visible and under 5% in normal play.

tasks.title: Cloud fallback decision and ADR
tasks.detail: SS15.6: local-only, or optional cloud for players without VRAM.
tasks.acceptance: An ADR recording the decision and its consequences for latency and privacy.

tasks.title: M6 evidence: stubbed versus live equivalence
tasks.detail: Run both, diff the state hashes, capture the result.
tasks.acceptance: Diff output uploaded as milestone evidence.

tasks.title: Model evaluation harness
tasks.detail: Compare candidate models on the actual prompts, measuring latency and refusal rate.
tasks.acceptance: Three models compared on the same 200 prompts with a written recommendation.

tasks.title: Dialogue content pipeline
tasks.detail: Authored fallbacks need writing, versioning and coverage measurement.
tasks.acceptance: Every dialogue surface has at least three authored fallbacks.

tasks.title: Narration failure modes and graceful degradation
tasks.detail: Model missing, VRAM exhausted, service crashed. All three must be survivable.
tasks.acceptance: Killing the narration service mid-conversation degrades to authored text.

tasks.title: Market instrument design and ADR
tasks.detail: SS15.5: order book, continuous double auction, or corp shares only. This determines the anti-bot surface.
tasks.acceptance: An ADR with the decision and the exploit surface it accepts.

tasks.title: Commodity supply and demand model
tasks.detail: Production, consumption and stock per region, moved by lanes.
tasks.acceptance: A blocked lane produces a shortage downstream within a legible number of ticks.

tasks.title: Price formation from supply and demand
tasks.detail: simulation event to supply/demand to price. Never the inverse.
tasks.acceptance: No price moves without a simulation event that caused it, asserted in a test.

tasks.title: Corporate balance sheets and share instruments
tasks.detail: Assets, liabilities, and shares outstanding that stay constant per instrument.
tasks.acceptance: Total shares outstanding per instrument is invariant over 1,000,000 ticks.

tasks.title: Faucets and sinks, explicitly logged
tasks.detail: Money supply changes only through defined faucets and sinks, and they are logged.
tasks.acceptance: Every change to the money supply names its faucet or sink in the event log.

tasks.title: Bankruptcy and asset transfer to creditors
tasks.detail: Assets transfer; they never delete. The state space is a cycle, not a line.
tasks.acceptance: A bankrupt corp's assets sum to the same total after the transfer as before.

tasks.title: Mean-reversion pressure at scale
tasks.detail: Overhead rises with size; rivals coalesce against a leader.
tasks.acceptance: Gini over lane holdings oscillates rather than trending over 1,000,000 ticks.

tasks.title: News feed UI with source bias
tasks.detail: Some outlets are captured. Corporate releases spin.
tasks.acceptance: Two outlets report the same event differently, and both are wrong in different ways.

tasks.title: Article lag behind price movement
tasks.detail: Players who watched the convoy die traded before the news broke.
tasks.acceptance: Articles are published a measurable number of ticks after the causing event.

tasks.title: Player trading interface
tasks.detail: Positions, orders, and a portfolio, in the instrument the ADR chose.
tasks.acceptance: A player can take a position on a corp and realise a gain from a simulated event.

tasks.title: Anti-bot friction, designed not discovered
tasks.detail: Knowledge that only exists inside physical conversations; positions requiring presence.
tasks.acceptance: A scripted client with full market data cannot outperform a player who travels.

tasks.title: Tier 3 fuzz over the economy for 1,000,000 ticks
tasks.detail: Adversarial scripted agent, every invariant asserted continuously, nightly in CI.
tasks.acceptance: The nightly run is green for seven consecutive nights.

tasks.title: Economy metrics dashboard
tasks.detail: Per-region tick cost, Gini, dominance, money supply, faucet and sink volumes.
tasks.acceptance: All SS12 economy metrics are visible on one page and alert outside their bands.

tasks.title: Cornering and manipulation testing
tasks.detail: Try to corner a market deliberately and see whether the invariants hold.
tasks.acceptance: A deliberate corner attempt is either impossible or self-correcting within N ticks.

tasks.title: M7 evidence: trade ahead of the news
tasks.detail: Record watching a convoy die, taking a position, and the article arriving late.
tasks.acceptance: Recording uploaded as milestone evidence.

tasks.title: Market UI: charts that do not lie
tasks.detail: Price history with the event that caused each move annotatable.
tasks.acceptance: A player can click a price move and see the article about it.

tasks.title: Economic tuning harness
tasks.detail: Run parameter sweeps headless and report which land inside the SS12 bands.
tasks.acceptance: A sweep of 200 parameter sets reports the viable region.

tasks.title: Economist review of the model
tasks.detail: SS6.5's prior-art warning is explicit: EVE employs professional economists.
tasks.acceptance: Written review on file with the failure modes it identifies.

tasks.title: Crew as first-class simulated entities
tasks.detail: Design SS2.1: crew are the losable thing. They hold beliefs, owe favours, and have their own fears. Not a stat block attached to the player.
tasks.acceptance: A crew member has a full belief set and can be queried like any other entity.

tasks.title: Hiring: finding, negotiating, and the terms
tasks.detail: Who is available depends on who has heard of you and what they believe.
tasks.acceptance: A crew member with a bad belief about the player refuses, and says why.

tasks.title: Crew skills as access rather than numbers
tasks.detail: A crew member's value is which obligation classes they unlock, not a damage modifier.
tasks.acceptance: Hiring a port authority contact opens clean landings that were previously unavailable.

tasks.title: Crew loyalty derived from obligations, not a bar
tasks.detail: Loyalty is computed from the favour ledger and the belief graph.
tasks.acceptance: grep for a loyalty scalar: zero hits. Loyalty is a query.

tasks.title: Crew can be bought, frightened, or turned
tasks.detail: A rival can approach your crew with money, a threat, or information.
tasks.acceptance: A rival successfully turns a crew member, and the player can find out how.

tasks.title: Crew death and its permanence
tasks.detail: SS15.4 is open: how permanent, and is there a mitigation the player can buy?
tasks.acceptance: An ADR recording the decision, and the behaviour matching it.

tasks.title: Crew presence in the world
tasks.detail: Crew appear aboard the ship and in the town, positioned from sim state.
tasks.acceptance: A crew member the sim says is at the town is standing in the town.

tasks.title: Crew dialogue driven by their own beliefs
tasks.detail: They tell you what they think is true, which is sometimes wrong.
tasks.acceptance: A crew member reports a stale location sincerely.

tasks.title: Crew-initiated missions
tasks.detail: NPCs call in favours on the player. SS6.2 says this is not optional content.
tasks.acceptance: A crew member's creditor calls in a favour and it becomes a contract the player must answer.

tasks.title: Crew roster UI
tasks.detail: Who you have, what they open, what they are owed and by whom.
tasks.acceptance: The roster shows obligations in both directions, not a loyalty percentage.

tasks.title: Crew jeopardy in mission resolution
tasks.detail: Bringing crew on a job risks them. The risk is legible before committing.
tasks.acceptance: The player can see, before accepting, which crew are exposed and to what.

tasks.title: M8 evidence: losing someone
tasks.detail: Record a chain of events ending in a crew loss that the player caused and could have foreseen, and the reconstruction afterwards.
tasks.acceptance: Recording plus the causal chain from the log, uploaded as milestone evidence.

tasks.title: Character rendering and variation
tasks.detail: Crew and NPCs need bodies that differ. Procedural variation over a base mesh.
tasks.acceptance: Twenty NPCs in one scene, visually distinguishable, at no measurable cost.

tasks.title: Character animation: idle, walk, sit, gesture
tasks.detail: Enough that a person standing in a bar reads as a person.
tasks.acceptance: An NPC transitions between states without a pop.

tasks.title: Crew audio: voice barks from the narration layer
tasks.detail: Short lines, generated text, synthesised or authored.
tasks.acceptance: A crew member's bark reflects a belief they actually hold.

tasks.title: Audit archetype on the shared algorithm
tasks.detail: Hidden variable: who is skimming. Resolution verb: expose or blackmail.
tasks.acceptance: Audit uses the identical investigation code path as Bounty, asserted by a test.

tasks.title: Interception archetype
tasks.detail: Hidden variable: route and timing. Resolution: board, destroy or observe.
tasks.acceptance: Interception constrains a search volume over route-time rather than position, using the same algorithm.

tasks.title: Extraction archetype
tasks.detail: Hidden variable: holding location. Resolution: retrieve a person or data.
tasks.acceptance: Extraction resolves against a physically present target.

tasks.title: Fabrication archetype
tasks.detail: No hidden variable: this one injects. Plant a false belief through the same pipeline the truth uses.
tasks.acceptance: A fabricated belief propagates identically to a true one and carries Provenance::Fabricated.

tasks.title: Collection archetype
tasks.detail: Hidden variable: debtor whereabouts and assets. Resolution: coerce or negotiate.
tasks.acceptance: Collection surfaces the debtor's assets as a second hidden variable.

tasks.title: Generalise the search volume beyond regions
tasks.detail: The algorithm currently constrains over RegionId. Make the hidden variable generic so route-time and identity work without a second implementation.
tasks.acceptance: One generic implementation serves all six archetypes; the old one is deleted.

tasks.title: Archetype distribution metric in CI
tasks.detail: SS12's oatmeal detector, asserted rather than observed.
tasks.acceptance: A 10,000 tick run fails CI if any archetype exceeds 35%.

tasks.title: Mission variety from simulation state, not templates
tasks.detail: Verify the variety comes from the world. Freeze the sim and confirm the generator produces almost nothing.
tasks.acceptance: With a static world, contract variety collapses; with a live one it does not.

tasks.title: Contract chaining and consequence
tasks.detail: Resolving one contract creates the tension the next one queries.
tasks.acceptance: A resolved contract is traceably the cause of a later one.

tasks.title: Difficulty from access rather than numbers
tasks.detail: A hard job is one you lack the obligation classes for, not one with more hit points.
tasks.acceptance: Two contracts with identical parameters differ in difficulty by the player's ledger.

tasks.title: M9 evidence: six archetypes, one code path
tasks.detail: Capture one contract of each type, plus the test asserting the shared path.
tasks.acceptance: Six recordings and the test output uploaded as milestone evidence.

tasks.title: Mission generation tuning harness
tasks.detail: Sweep the query parameters and report archetype distribution and tension age.
tasks.acceptance: A sweep reports which parameters keep every archetype under 35%.

tasks.title: Second external playtest, full loop
tasks.detail: Six archetypes, live economy, crew. Watch for the oatmeal problem.
tasks.acceptance: Five sessions, with players asked to describe two contracts they did.

tasks.title: Content pass on contract presentation
tasks.detail: The board text has to carry the tension. Written from state, not templated.
tasks.acceptance: No two contracts on the board read as the same sentence with names swapped.

tasks.title: Aggregate region representation
tasks.detail: Distant regions tick statistically: aggregate flows, no individual agents.
tasks.acceptance: A region with no observer costs under 0.05 ms per tick.

tasks.title: Reification: aggregate to concrete agents
tasks.detail: When a player arrives, approximate state instantiates into individuals consistently.
tasks.acceptance: Arriving at a region twice from the same aggregate state produces the same agents.

tasks.title: Dereification: concrete back to aggregate
tasks.detail: When they leave, concrete state folds back without losing information.
tasks.acceptance: Property test: aggregate(reify(A)) == A for arbitrary aggregate state.

tasks.title: Concurrent arrival determinism
tasks.detail: SS15.3 is open: two players entering a statistical region simultaneously. Who triggers the transform, and is it deterministic?
tasks.acceptance: An ADR, and a test with two simultaneous arrivals producing one consistent result.

tasks.title: Belief propagation across the LOD boundary
tasks.detail: A rumour must cross from aggregate to concrete and back without being lost or doubled.
tasks.acceptance: A belief injected in an aggregate region is present after reification, at the right confidence.

tasks.title: Per-region tick cost budget and enforcement
tasks.detail: SS12: under 5 ms full fidelity. Measure per region and alert.
tasks.acceptance: The metrics dashboard shows per-region cost and flags any region over budget.

tasks.title: Server cost per region-tick, measured
tasks.detail: SS14 R7: simulation cost scales with world size, not player count. Know the number.
tasks.acceptance: Cost per region-tick is reported continuously and tracked over time.

tasks.title: Scale to 2,000 simulated entities across 5 regions
tasks.detail: The MVP scale from SS3, running with LOD.
tasks.acceptance: 2,000 entities, 5 regions, under 5 ms per full-fidelity region tick.

tasks.title: Seam hunting: find the LOD boundary as a player
tasks.detail: Fly between regions repeatedly and try to catch the transform.
tasks.acceptance: No observable discontinuity in entity behaviour across 50 crossings.

tasks.title: M10 evidence: the reification property test
tasks.detail: Capture the property test output over 100,000 arbitrary aggregate states.
tasks.acceptance: Test output uploaded as milestone evidence.

tasks.title: Memory profiling at MVP scale
tasks.detail: 2,000 entities, five regions, and a planet. Know where the memory goes.
tasks.acceptance: A memory report attributing every 10 MB to a subsystem.

tasks.title: Sim performance optimisation pass
tasks.detail: Profile the tick and cut the top three costs.
tasks.acceptance: Per-region full-fidelity tick under 5 ms with 400 entities present.

tasks.title: Save and load a whole world
tasks.detail: Snapshot plus log, restored to a bit-identical state.
tasks.acceptance: A save restored on another machine produces the same state fingerprint.

tasks.title: IP counsel review against SS6.1 and SS6.10
tasks.detail: SS7 requires this before Phase 2. The Nemesis patent expires August 2036; our differentiator is structural, not cosmetic.
tasks.acceptance: Written counsel opinion on file, and any required changes implemented.

tasks.title: Sim-authoritative multiplayer session
tasks.detail: One shard, sim owns all world state, clients hold views.
tasks.acceptance: Two clients see the same world state and cannot disagree about it.

tasks.title: Target persistence classes
tasks.detail: SS15.2 is open. Unique, Regional and Personal, declared on the contract board.
tasks.acceptance: An ADR, and the board declaring the class of every contract up front.

tasks.title: Contested targets and intentional races
tasks.detail: A Unique target is shared and the race is the point.
tasks.acceptance: Two players hunting one target both see it move, and only one can resolve it.

tasks.title: Fabrication rate limits and traceability
tasks.detail: SS6.10: rumour injection is a griefing surface. Rate-limit per source, require corroboration above a confidence ceiling.
tasks.acceptance: A coordinated injection attempt by four accounts fails to move a target's standing past the ceiling.

tasks.title: Client-predicted combat with server validation
tasks.detail: Standard posture per SS6.10. No custom netcode before MVP.
tasks.acceptance: Combat feels responsive at 120 ms RTT and the server rejects impossible outcomes.

tasks.title: Presence and region handoff
tasks.detail: Players entering and leaving regions drive the LOD transform correctly.
tasks.acceptance: Sixteen players spread across five regions with correct fidelity in each.

tasks.title: Shard topology decision and ADR
tasks.detail: SS15.7: one shard or several with separate world state? It decides whether the world that lives without you is one world or many.
tasks.acceptance: An ADR with the decision and its consequence for the premise.

tasks.title: Sixteen-player soak test
tasks.detail: Sixteen clients, one hour, scripted behaviour plus humans.
tasks.acceptance: No desync, no crash, no duplicated target, memory flat.

tasks.title: Server cost model at 32 players
tasks.detail: Measure what a shard actually costs, so the revenue relationship is known.
tasks.acceptance: Cost per player-hour reported, with the region-tick component separated out.

tasks.title: M11 evidence: sixteen players, one hour
tasks.detail: Record the soak test with the server metrics alongside.
tasks.acceptance: Recording and metrics uploaded as milestone evidence.

tasks.title: Account and identity handling
tasks.detail: Who a player is, minimally and safely. No credentials stored by us.
tasks.acceptance: Sign-in works and stores no password or payment data.

tasks.title: Anti-cheat posture for a sim-authoritative world
tasks.detail: The sim owns state, so cheating means lying about intents. Validate them.
tasks.acceptance: A client sending impossible intents is disconnected and logged.

tasks.title: Griefing review across every system
tasks.detail: Not only rumour injection: contracts, markets, crew, and presence.
tasks.acceptance: A written review naming each surface and its mitigation.

tasks.title: Third external playtest, multiplayer
tasks.detail: Sixteen people who do not know each other.
tasks.acceptance: Written notes, plus the belief graph state before and after.

tasks.title: Pillar P1: the world does not wait for you
tasks.detail: Log out for a week of world time. Come back. Find three specific, causally-explicable changes that had nothing to do with you.
tasks.acceptance: Three changes found and each traced to its cause in the log.

tasks.title: Pillar P2: consequence legible in hindsight
tasks.detail: Take any world-state change and reconstruct the four preceding causes from information available in-game before it happened.
tasks.acceptance: Four causes reconstructed from in-game information only, not from the event log.

tasks.title: Pillar P3: knowledge is asymmetric
tasks.detail: Two players in the same system holding contradictory, sincerely-held, non-buggy beliefs about the same fact.
tasks.acceptance: Two players demonstrate the contradiction and both can justify their belief.

tasks.title: Pillar P4: you are a participant, not a protagonist
tasks.detail: A player permanently loses something they spent twenty hours building, through a chain that was their fault and was foreseeable.
tasks.acceptance: The loss happens, and the player can name the decision that caused it.

tasks.title: Full SS12 metrics run at MVP scale
tasks.detail: Every metric in the band, on a live build, with real players.
tasks.acceptance: All nine SS12 metrics inside their target ranges over a 24-hour live run.

tasks.title: Fresh-agent review pass over the whole codebase
tasks.detail: SS8.7, capped at two rounds. Fresh context, checking against SS8.1 to SS8.6 and every invariant in SS6.
tasks.acceptance: Two rounds complete; everything surviving is recorded as a judgement call.

tasks.title: Architecture documentation refresh
tasks.detail: Every ADR current, every architecture doc matching the code.
tasks.acceptance: No ADR describes a decision that has since been reversed without a superseding ADR.

tasks.title: MVP gate review and go/no-go
tasks.detail: The four pillar tests, the metrics, and an honest assessment of Phase 3 feasibility.
tasks.acceptance: A written gate decision with evidence for each pillar.

tasks.title: M12 evidence: the four pillar tests
tasks.detail: Capture each pillar test being passed, with the supporting reconstruction.
tasks.acceptance: Four recordings and their causal chains uploaded as milestone evidence.

tasks.title: Release build and packaging pipeline
tasks.detail: Cook, package, sign and distribute a build people can install.
tasks.acceptance: A tester installs and runs the build with no engine present.

tasks.title: Telemetry for the pillar tests in the wild
tasks.detail: Instrument the four pillars so they can be measured on real sessions.
tasks.acceptance: Each pillar has a metric that can be read off a live population.

tasks.title: Phase 3 assessment and funding materials
tasks.detail: SS13.5 is explicit that Phase 3 is not achievable solo. Phase 2 exists to be the thing you raise money or recruit on.
tasks.acceptance: A written assessment with the metrics and recordings that support it.
